spans.s: garbha (LL), a cell; cf. pañca-garbha (LL), ‘a five-celled building’; nava-garbha (LL), ‘a nine-celled building’; sapta-garbha (LL), ‘seven-celled building’.
garbh-āgāra (CII 1), the inner apartment of a temple or palace; same as garbha-gṛha.
garbha-gṛha (SITI), the innermost sanctuary of a temple; inner part of palace; same as garbh-āgāra.
Garga-yavana (EI 33), name applied to the Turkish Muslim invaders of North India, Garga probably being Ghaznī.
garta, gartā (EI 3, 27; CII 3), a trench or pit; a boundary trench; a pit or valley; cf. sa-gart-oṣara (IE 8-5); also found as the termination of names of villages.
garuḍa (IA 20), the royal eagle; the white kite (in areas like Bihar and Madras).
